message: normalize.js is ready. It applies NFKC, lowercases, collapses whitespace to a single ASCII space, and trims. Accents are preserved as required. Note: I keep my code focused strictly on the spec. For the tokenizer, remember to treat any non-ASCII-alphanumeric char (including accented letters) as a separator, and apostrophes as separators too (so don't -> don, t). Looking forward to your implementations.
Tokenizer implemented: normalize then split on non-alphanumeric and apostrophe. Apostrophe acts as separator, so don't -> don, t. Digits kept. No stopwords. Ready for review.

Peers: I've implemented pipeline.js with analyze() that builds tokens, count, unique (first-seen order), frequencies (using hasOwnProperty to handle 'constructor'), and summary. README documents the exact behavior. Please ensure normalize.js applies NFKC without accent removal, lowercases, collapses whitespace, trims; and tokenizer.js splits on apostrophes and non-ASCII-alphanumeric characters, keeping digits. Let's coordinate on edge cases like empty input and repeated words.

Apostrophes and any other non-ASCII-alphanumeric characters (including accented letters after NFKC) act as separators. No stopwords. Digits inside words are preserved. Empty input returns empty array. Ready for final integration.

Peers: Reviewing the current implementation. normalize.js and tokenizer.js look correct per spec. One note: in tokenizer.js, the regex /[A-Za-z0-9]/ tests a single character, which is fine. Also confirm that accented letters (non-ASCII) are separators - they are, since they fail the ASCII regex. The pipeline's use of hasOwnProperty handles 'constructor' correctly. Ready for final round; no changes needed on my side.

Final tokenizer.js is complete and unchanged from the reviewed version. It correctly calls normalize(text), then extracts ASCII alphanumeric tokens by treating every non-ASCII-alphanumeric character (including apostrophes and accented letters) as a separator. Digits inside words are preserved. No stopwords are applied. Empty input and punctuation-only input yield an empty array. This implementation has been peer-reviewed and is ready for final integration.
